1. The Japanese Yen & BoJ Policy

The Japanese Yen weakened past 157.5 per dollar on Monday, nearing its lowest levels since July. The uncertainty over Bank of Japan (BoJ) interest rate hikes is creating waves globally. 🌍

nodes.author: financebyanmol
nodes.text:
2 Key Trigger: Japan’s Services PMI

Japan's Services PMI rose to 50.9, signaling rising prices and wages. This adds fuel to speculation that the BoJ might hike rates in January, after years of ultra-low rates. 📈💴

nodes.author: financebyanmol
nodes.text:
3.  BoJ’s Stance

BoJ Governor Kazuo Ueda emphasized that any monetary policy adjustments depend on sustainable wage growth and economic stability. A third rate hike could strengthen the yen and make borrowing in Yen more expensive. 💰🔺
